In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic and biochemical characterization of mutants defective in CDP-digliceride synthetase, the enzyme which catalyzes the first committed step in phospholipid synthesis.

the identification of the gene(s) involved in the synthesis and degradation of phosphatidylglycerol and the role of this phospholipid in the maintenance of the proton gradient across the cytoplasmic membrane.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the CDP-diglceride synthetase of Escherichi coli K-12 is subject to pH control, that the pH-sensitive cds-8 mutant is suppressed by mutations at the cdsS locus, and that the cdsS gene product is involved in the pH regulation of synthetase activity.
mutations in the cdss gene suppress the pH-sensitivity of a cds mutant by inhibiting the inactivation of the residual synthetase activity.
a mutation in cdsS gene can suppress the growth defect of cds mutants at high pH, and the mechanism of suppression is to prevent the decay of residual enzyme activity at high pH.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cds locus is involved in regulating the synthesis of CDP-dg and that the cdsS locus is involved in maintaining the activity of CDP-dG synthetase at a high level in the presence of a cds mutation.
a cds mutation is not lethal per se but causes the pH sensitivity of cells by decreasing the level of CDF-diglyceride synthesis.
the cds locus is a regulatory locus and that the cdsS locus is a suppressor locus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CDP-diglyc- eride synthetase gene (cds) is a pH-sensitive locus and the cdsS gene is a pH suppressor.
the cdsS gene product appears to play a critical role in the maintenance of CDP-dgyceride synthetase in an active state.
